summary: The bill requires all naturalization applicants to swear under penalty of perjury that they have not committed and do not intend to commit any of dozens of listed federal terrorism offenses, adds the same disavowal to the oath of allegiance, and creates new presumptions and procedures allowing the government to revoke citizenship and deport any naturalized person later convicted of or credibly shown to have engaged in such offenses.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends immigration and naturalization procedures under the INA but contains no provisions that authorize, appropriate, or alter any federal spending, programs, or budgets. It focuses exclusively on eligibility requirements, attestations, and revocation processes.
No provisions address tax rates, credits, deductions, enforcement, or any revenue-related matters.
The legislation does not reference healthcare access, coverage, providers, or any public/private healthcare systems.
No provisions relate to firearms, background checks, restrictions, or Second Amendment issues.

The bill is primarily and directly about immigration. It adds a mandatory terrorism-disavowal attestation to naturalization (Form N-400 and oath), creates new grounds and presumptions for denaturalization based on terrorism-related convictions or conduct, mandates deportation after revocation, imposes permanent inadmissibility bars, revokes all immigration benefits/status, and eliminates waivers. These changes strictly limit pathways to citizenship and presence in the U.S. for individuals linked to covered terrorism offenses, aligning strongly with restricting immigration and enforcing borders.
No provisions address reproductive rights, abortion access, or related regulations.
No provisions authorize, modify, or affect military or defense appropriations or policy.
No provisions relate to environmental regulations, protections, or climate policy.
No provisions address welfare programs, food assistance, or other safety-net benefits.
No provisions address schools, funding, choice, or federal education policy.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.

The bill leverages criminal convictions for covered terrorism offenses as triggers for denaturalization and removal, creating presumptions of illegal procurement and expanding civil proceedings. This has a tangential, minor alignment with tougher enforcement consequences but does not alter sentencing, policing, rehabilitation, or general criminal procedure.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
No provisions address deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
No provisions address legal protections or rights for LGBTQ+ individuals.
No provisions address foreign assistance or aid programs.
No provisions address voting access, voter ID, or election procedures.
No provisions address data privacy, tech regulation, or surveillance.
No provisions address worker protections, unions, or employment policy.
No provisions address religious exemptions, civil rights, or anti-discrimination laws.
